title: Empirical Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Loop for Intent→Network Configuration Using a Deterministic Reachability Validator
abstract: We present a fully preregistered, artifact‑archived paired experiment that measures the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic reachability validator + ≤1 automated repair (the guarded GVR loop) around a single LLM generator (declared gpt‑5‑mini) for intent→device‑configuration NetOps tasks. Using a shared‑initial paired design (preregistration cns‑m2026‑01), we ran 300 distinct intents (600 episodes). Baseline (generator candidate) execution‑validated correctness = 299/300 (99.667%); guarded pipeline = 300/300 (100.0%). Paired difference = 0.003333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider‑call accounting: 301 model calls (300 generator + 1 repair). All raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, per‑episode scoring JSONs, manifests, and SHA‑256 hashes are archived and cited in the Disclosure Statement. We describe the preregistered design, deterministic scoring semantics, full reconciliation accounting, representative artifact‑grounded examples, diagnostic failure taxonomy, threats to validity, and operational implications.

sections.introduction: Large language models are promising for translating operator intent into device configurations, but deployment requires mechanical guarantees that generated artifacts do not violate reachability, access control, or other safety invariants. A practical engineering pattern is generate→validate→(repair) where a deterministic validator gates execution and requests repairs when needed. We study the question stated in the preregistration (cns‑m2026‑01): Does a validator + ≤1 automated repair (GVR) increase the paired rate of execution‑validated correct configurations vs the plain LLM generator on a curated NetOps intent→configuration corpus? Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered paired evaluation with shared‑initial semantics and deterministic reconciliation; (2) an emulator‑backed deterministic validator and archived per‑episode validator traces and provider calls; (3) exact paired inference and bootstrap uncertainty with archived seeds and code; and (4) a failure‑mode taxonomy and operational discussion grounded in archived artifacts.
sections.related_work: Prior work has explored LLMs for intent→config synthesis, verifier‑assisted generation, and generate–validate–repair patterns in software and control domains. We position this study as an operationally focused, preregistered, reproducible measurement of the gating effect rather than a benchmark of generator quality across models. Representative references from our literature lead set include NetConf/intent papers and recent verifier‑assisted NetOps prototypes; we cite closest contextual leads in the evidence bundle (see Cited Record Ids). Our method complements prior prototypes by (i) freezing analysis via preregistration (cns‑m2026‑01), (ii) deterministically simulating device effects for validator checks, and (iii) archiving every provider call and validator trace for deterministic reconciliation.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as cns‑m2026‑01 (preregistration SHA‑256: 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline in a shared‑initial paired design. The design fixed: task_bank N=300 intents, shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generator proposal per intent reused for baseline and guarded conditions), repair budget ≤1 automated repair call, contamination/exclusion rules, retry policy, stopping rules, and the analysis plan (exact McNemar two‑sided; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration and analysis code/seeds are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; see hashes in Disclosure).Task generation and contamination checks. A deterministic task generator produced 300 intent→configuration tasks combining filtered public examples and seeded synthetic templates. Deterministic contamination heuristics (exact strings and k‑token shingle overlap) excluded flagged items; the final manifest is archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256: 91564bb6...).Shared‑initial paired semantics. To isolate the validator+repair marginal effect, each intent used a single generator proposal that served both as the baseline output and as the guarded pipeline input. This choice reduces generator variance across conditions and attributes outcome differences to the validator/repair stage rather than to stochastic generator sampling.Generator and validator. Declared generator: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: a40e96e2...). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) parses candidates, simulates deterministic state transitions on an archived emulator snapshot, enforces task constraints (allowed_touched_fields, group constraints, preserve_unspecified_state), and returns structured pass/fail results plus a validator trace. On validator failure the pipeline permits one automated repair call (preregistered). All model calls and validator traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/scoring/.Scoring and inferential method. Per intent outcome = 1 if the validator reports an execution‑validated configuration satisfying the intent with no unintended reachability/policy changes; else 0. The primary test is the exact McNemar two‑sided on paired discordant counts (n10,n01). We additionally report a paired bootstrap percentile CI for the guarded−baseline difference using 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729 (archived). Reproducibility: raw outputs, per‑call provider traces, per‑episode scoring JSONs, and the full reconciliation manifest are archived and SHA‑256 hashed (see Disclosure).
sections.results: Execution summary and reconciliation. Planned episodes = 600 (300 intents × shared initial). Completed episodes = 600; technical failures = 0. Model calls recorded = 301 total (300 generator calls + 1 repair call). Raw run results: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256: 176776d1...). Deterministic reconciliation and provider audit: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256: f6da5050...).Primary outcomes and inferential results. Aggregates (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256: 55eacb88...): baseline successes = 299/300 (0.996667); guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256: 3421adb5...): n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333333333332993. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The analysis artifacts and seeds are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256: 7db06f53...).Interpretation of the p‑value. With small discordant counts (n10=1, n01=0) the exact two‑sided McNemar implementation used in the archived analysis yields p = 1.0; our archived analysis code and seeds permit external verification and alternative exact formulations if readers prefer different two‑sided enumeration conventions. The bootstrap CI bounds the paired difference to ≤1% at 95% confidence in this corpus.Diagnostic and repair details. A single automated repair call was invoked and archived (execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json SHA‑256: 4deb410d...). That repair corrected the lone baseline failure. Across the run we observed no validator false negatives. Representative per‑episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/) include validator violation codes, parsed_command_count, and touched field counts (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256: 2e4a1ef1..., execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json SHA‑256: 635b97a3...). Figures and tables (captions archived) summarize repair counts, contingency counts, and the failure‑mode taxonomy derived from validator diagnostics.
sections.discussion: Bounded operational inference. In this archived emulator corpus the generator performed near ceiling; the guarded GVR pattern corrected the single baseline error at the cost of one extra model call (301 total). This demonstrates that a deterministic validator + a small automated repair budget can reduce residual generator errors at low incremental cost when generator quality is already high. It does not imply that the guarded pattern will always produce large absolute gains in higher‑error distributions—those settings require larger budgets and different operational tradeoffs.Construct validity and externality. The deterministic validator operationalizes safety as absence of emulator‑observed unintended reachability/policy changes in a closed snapshot. This choice is reproducible and conservative for controlled evaluation, but it omits production dynamics such as hardware idiosyncrasies, multi‑domain live interactions, non‑deterministic timing effects, or cross‑controller state. Shared‑initial semantics isolates the validator’s marginal effect but does not evaluate pipelines in which the guarded condition causes a different generator invocation strategy or context. Both design choices were preregistered and archived.Threats to internal validity. Prompt sensitivity and generator nondeterminism were mitigated by (i) using a single shared initial candidate per intent and (ii) archiving raw generator outputs and provider traces. The shared‑initial design reduces within‑pair variance but prevents evaluation of multi‑query guarded designs. Missingness and exclusions. No technical exclusions occurred: completed episodes = planned episodes = 600; excluded tasks due to contamination were removed prior to final selection per preregistered deterministic rules (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256: 91564bb6...).Operational implications. For NetOps integrators, the guarded pattern can function as a low‑cost safety gate when generator quality is high: a deterministic validator turns soft‑semantic correctness into a reproducible pass/fail, and a constrained repair budget can catch occasional omissions. However, deployments with larger generator error rates will need to budget verification latency and assess robustness of the validator across heterogeneous device/firmware stacks.Reproducibility. Every run artifact required to reproduce the analysis is archived and SHA‑256 hashed: execution/raw_results.jsonl (176776d1...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (91564bb6...), execution/model_configuration.json (a40e96e2...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (3421adb5...), analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (f6da5050...), repair trace (4deb410d...). The initial master prompt archive path and SHA are listed in the Disclosure. The analysis seeds and the exact analysis log are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256: 7db06f53...).
sections.conclusion: A fully preregistered, artifact‑archived shared‑initial paired experiment (cns‑m2026‑01) found that, on a 300‑intent emulator corpus, a deterministic validator plus ≤1 automated repair corrected the single residual generator failure at the cost of a single extra model call (301 total). Observed counts: baseline 299/300, guarded 300/300; paired difference 0.00333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The results are artifact‑grounded; all provider and validator traces and cryptographic hashes are archived for deterministic reproduction. The guarded GVR loop is operationally useful under high baseline quality and low verification cost; broader claims about production benefit under different generator error regimes or adversarial distributions require further preregistered evaluation using the same archival discipline.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (archived references and runtime facts)

Initial master prompt (immutable archive): provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
Preregistration: study_id = cns‑m2026‑01 (frozen plan) — preregistration SHA‑256: 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7. The preregistration fixed the primary estimand, paired shared‑initial design, repair budget (≤1), retry policy, contamination/exclusion rules, and the exact analysis plan (exact McNemar two‑sided; paired bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Declared model(s) and config: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider family: recorded in execution/provider_calls/ (full per‑call traces archived for every model invocation).

Orchestration and validation framework: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator v5.0) implemented to parse candidates, simulate deterministic device state transitions in an archived emulator snapshot, check task and group constraints, and deterministically return pass/fail with structured traces. Repair policy: a single automated repair attempt permitted on validator failure (preregistered). Representative repair trace: execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256: 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba.

Primary run artifacts (representative):
- Raw run results: execution/raw_results.jsonl — SHA‑256: 176776d1c015a652ea2d28ced2be39ffbfec9b969b72ab03e1a1193b567b6dbb.
- Task manifest (N=300): execution/task_manifest.jsonl — SHA‑256: 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990.
- Analysis log and exact analysis seeds/params: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl — SHA‑256: 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e.
- Paired contingency CSV used for the confirmatory test: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv — SHA‑256: 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55.
- Deterministic reconciliation and provider call audit: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json — SHA‑256: f6da505032ab388ceccda8e85084b53b8cada91a7ccc0dc65601385505f00ea6.
- Representative per‑episode artifacts (pair‑000001 example): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt — SHA‑256: 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json — SHA‑256: 2e4a1ef1389a18cfc5a0d6728d0978879c6675125b090b66c2dbd97b730ef153.

Run accounting and deviations. The execution manifest records: planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 301 (300 generator + 1 repair). All provider calls and call cache entries are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/ with per‑file SHA‑256s (full manifest available at execution/execution_manifest.json). No manual, post‑lock edits were made to substantive manuscript content; all manuscript text describing run design and outcomes derives from the archived autonomous run artifacts.

Limitations (summary): single declared LLM (no multi‑model claim); deterministic emulator validator abstracts production dynamics and may not capture live multi‑domain behaviors; shared‑initial semantics isolates gate marginal effect but does not measure pipelines that requery the generator differently per condition; repair budget limited to one automated attempt. See manuscript Limitations for full discussion.

I certify these artifact paths and SHA‑256 values are copied from the archived autonomous run and are not invented.
limitations: High baseline ceiling (baseline = 299/300) reduces statistical power to detect small practical effects; the run nevertheless reports exact paired counts and bootstrap CI.

Construct validity: the deterministic emulator validator operationalizes safety as absence of emulator‑observed unintended reachability/policy changes in a closed snapshot; production exposures (hardware variants, cross‑domain live interactions) exceed this scope.
Model scope: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini); no claim of multi‑model generality.
Design semantics: shared‑initial design isolates the validator marginal effect but does not evaluate pipelines that independently requery the LLM per condition.
Repair budget: only one automated repair attempt permitted; iterative multi‑call repair strategies were not evaluated in this confirmatory run.
